statement_refuted: There is a law-uniform finite bound on the conditional 3-dimensional density of three selected large spectral coordinates given all remaining spectral coordinates, under only independent original-coordinate densities bounded by one.
counterexample: For iid Uniform[0,1]^4, choose an orthogonal spectral basis with Z=(X1+X2+X3+X4)/2. For 0<z<1/2 the orthogonal cube slice has 3-volume V(z)=8 z^3/3, hence the conditional density of the other three orthogonal coordinates has essential supremum 3/(8 z^3), which diverges as z->0. Taking A=O^T diag(1,1,-1,0) O places the construction in the exact three-large-eigenvalue target.
scope_note: This does not refute QFORM or rank-three coarea itself. It refutes taking a uniform conditional projection-density cap before averaging. The weighted quantity p_Z(z)||rho_{Y|Z=z}||inf equals the fiber supremum and is subject to the existing fiber-sup dimension-loss obstruction.
